sources.quote: In 2025, over 42,000 Texans accessed abortion via telehealth from shield law providers, a substantial increase from the 12,400 who did so in 2023.
sources.searcher_note: Guttmacher's own release on the same study; annual 2025 vs 2023, not Jan-Mar 2026 vs Jan-Mar 2024. Post-cutoff date.

sources.quote: In 2025, approximately 42,000 Texans accessed telehealth abortion care under the protection of shield laws, a substantial increase from the 12,400 who did so in 2023.
sources.searcher_note: Full report behind the release above; page shows 'July 2026' with no day. Also says Texans travelling out of state dropped by more than 10,000.

sources.quote: Despite Texas having one of the most restrictive abortion bans in the country, more than 41,000 residents had clinician-provided abortions in 2025, an over 20% jump from 2024.
sources.searcher_note: News story on Guttmacher monthly study data, quotes Guttmacher's Isaac Maddow-Zimet; year 2025 vs 2024, rising direction.

sources.quote: The estimated total number of abortions obtained by Texas residents went from 52,495 in 2021 to 56,350 in 2023 and 64,060 in 2024.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff piece citing Guttmacher; counts Texas residents anywhere (travel + telehealth), annual through 2024, a different definition from the lead's monthly in-state count. Type may be commentary; judge should check.

sources.quote: while in 2024, 74,000 people living in states with total bans traveled out of their state to access care, this dropped to 62,000 in 2025
sources.searcher_note: Full-year 2025 estimates (page shows March 2026); ban states overall, telehealth up 74,000 to 91,000. Pattern, no Texas line quoted.

notes: Every Texas source found reports rising telehealth abortions, but on annual windows (2025 vs 2024 or 2023). None found gives the Jan-Mar 2026 3,530/month figure, the +26% vs Jan-Mar 2024, or the December 2024 jump / range method seam. A search snippet cited #WeCount (Society of Family Planning, not Guttmacher) at an average 3,427 telehealth abortions a month in Texas in Q4 2024, via Axios Houston 2025-08-08 (https://www.axios.com/local/houston/2025/08/08/post-dobbs-abortions-rise-in-texas), but that page returned 403, so no quote. The Live Action #WeCount piece returned 429. No source found says Texas numbers fell in 2026.
